summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): Madrid (Chueca): among the most visible LGBT urban scenes in Europe; total anonymity in daily life; Pride among the continent's largest. Regional evidence: the one community that has used its own legislative power to narrow trans law - Ley 17/2023 and Ley 18/2023 (both 27 December 2023) amended the community's own 2016 gender-identity law and its anti-LGBTBI law on the stated ground of protecting freedom of expression and academic freedom, stripping the provisions that obliged educational institutions; Ley 1/2022 centres parents as primary responsible parties and structures school opt-outs (the 'pin parental' mechanism in Madrid schools). Evidentiary caveat: Madrid's citizens report LGTBI hate-crime offences to reporting services more than any other community's, so low recorded hostility here is not available as an alibi - the divergence is statutory, not statistical. Scored relative to the national score (0.88) for Spain.

sources.summary: Official text (BOE) of Ley 4/2023 (28 February 2023), "for the real and effective equality of trans people and the guarantee of the rights of LGTBI people": establishes self-ID legal gender recognition (16+, no diagnosis), broad anti-discrimination guarantees, employment and health measures, and an LGTBI equality strategy. National framework that Madrid's 2023 amendments sit beside.

Human Rights Watch (Feb 2023): "Victory in Fight for Gender Recognition in Spain" - hails Spain's self-ID gender-recognition law as a hard-won victory after years of activism. National framework context.

Spanish criminal-law firm analysis (June 2026): disentangles three statutes - what Law 4/2023 does and does not do; the discrimination aggravating factor of Article 22.4 of the Penal Code (gender identity/expression motives); and the hate offences of Article 510 CP extended to trans/LGBTI people. National framework context.

localsOnly: Resident-facing: the 2023 community-level amendments that removed the 2016 trans-law obligations on educational institutions, and the 2022 education law's parental-primary-responsibility and school opt-out mechanism ("pin parental"), shape school environments for local families.
